## SECTION 1: "WHAT CHANGED"

Two high-novelty structural claims warrant attention. First, macro_alf (novelty: 7) argues FOMC Chair Warsh is actively *reframing Fed benchmarks* to justify sustained dovishness — not merely holding rates, but engineering a structural bias against hiking. If accurate, this invalidates any inflation-driven tightening thesis for the foreseeable term. Second, gold options skew has inverted (novelty: 7): downside puts are now pricing richer than upside calls for the first time in years, signaling institutional *underinvestment* in gold and a potential squeeze higher. The macro_alf "run it hot" framework (G20 fiscal + AI capex as twin inflationary engines) adds structural context but is lower novelty (5). Strait of Hormuz resolution flagged as the critical binary gating condition for the entire risk-on thesis.

## SECTION 3: "DIVERGENCES & BLIND SPOTS"

**[CONTRARIAN] — Gold Positioning vs. Bearish/Neutral Commodity Consensus**
Sources say gold is structurally underowned with options skew flipped bullish. General commodity consensus is only mildly bullish (+1.86). The skew inversion is a concrete, observable positioning signal — institutions have not loaded up on gold despite the "run it hot" macro regime being the base case. *Why it matters:* V16 should be checking gold (GLD/GC) positioning in the 25-asset universe. F6 could see unusual call volume in gold miners (GDX, NEM, GOLD) as institutions close the underweight. **Severity: 7/10.**

**[BLIND_SPOT] — Warsh Fed Dovishness vs. Market Inflation Pricing**
Sources (HIGH confidence, 4 sources) assert Warsh is structurally reframing benchmarks to avoid hiking. If market is still pricing any meaningful hiking probability, there is a tradeable divergence in rates/short-end. DOLLAR NO_DATA amplifies this blind spot — a dovish structural pivot should be USD-negative, but no dollar thesis is being tracked today. *Why it matters:* V16 regime detection should weight this against any hawkish-regime signals. Short 2Y or long TLT/duration could be the expression. **Severity: 7/10.**

**[CROWDED] — Bearish Europe / EU Deindustrialization**
ZeroHedge and others uniformly bearish on EU via wealth taxes, CBDC, green deindustrialization. This is a crowded, consensus short Europe trade. *Why it matters:* Crowded consensus = potential squeeze risk if any EU macro data surprises or political pivot occurs. Do not add fresh short European exposure without a catalyst. **Severity: 5/10.**

**[BLIND_SPOT] — Hormuz as Binary Macro Gate, Zero Tracking**
macro_alf explicitly flags Hormuz resolution as the single gating condition for the entire risk-on/run-it-hot framework. Ceasefire is described as fragile (ZH). Yet GEOPOLITICS scores nearly NEUTRAL (-0.16) and ENERGY is only moderately bearish. The system appears to be under-pricing the binary optionality here. *Why it matters:* An escalation re-opens energy disruption and invalidates equities/commodities bull thesis simultaneously. **Severity: 6/10.**
